title: How to Answer Support Emails in Intercom Inbox With AI
summary: Connect Quickchat AI to Intercom Inbox to answer support emails from your knowledge base. Use the workspace address or forward mail from your support mailbox.
body_markdown:
A customer emails your support team to ask how to pack a return. The instructions are already in a help article, so someone finds the right paragraph and writes back. If that question comes up often, you can give an AI teammate the same article and let it answer the emails you choose.


**Intercom Inbox** is the shared inbox where your team reads customer emails and decides who should reply. **Quickchat AI** connects to Intercom as a teammate. When you assign it a conversation, it can answer from the help articles and policies you give it.


You’ll run the support desk for **Wheelhouse Repair** , a fictional bike shop. A rider needs the return code for a broken light. Your goal is to open that email in Intercom and see a public answer with two details from the shop’s policy, the code and where to put the paper slip. Here’s what that looked like in our test.


The rider asked for a return code. In both Intercom and Quickchat AI, the answer gives LILAC-27 and tells the rider to put the paper slip inside the battery compartment.


You can try this with one external mailbox and the email address Intercom gives your workspace. If you followed our[Intercom Messenger handoff tutorial](https://quickchat.ai/post/intercom-chatbot-human-handoff) , reuse the same Agent, teammate and workspace.


[Download the repair policy, test emails and checks in one text file](https://quickchat.ai/blog-assets/downloads/intercom-email-pilot.txt)


## 1. Choose where the support email goes


The quickest route is to write directly to the workspace address, as we did. If customers already write to a company support address, the optional forwarding setup below lets them keep using it.


Use a regular Intercom workspace with Inbox access. If your team already handles live customer mail, choose a separate test workspace. To test delivery to a customer, the workspace must also be allowed to send outbound email.[Intercom workspace review](https://www.intercom.com/help/en/articles/567399-intercom-s-workspace-review-process) ·[Developer workspace limits](https://developers.intercom.com/docs/build-an-integration/getting-started)


### Try the built-in workspace address


In the Intercom owner’s window, open **Settings → Channels → Email → Email settings** and copy **Workspace email address** . Paste it into the **To** field of a new email in your external mailbox. With this address, you can skip the forwarding setup and go straight to “Find the customer’s email in Inbox” below.[Intercom’s workspace email address](https://www.intercom.com/help/en/articles/6522819-automatically-forward-emails-to-the-inbox)


Copy the address from Wheelhouse’s Email settings into the To field of a new email. The sender used an ordinary mail app to ask the shop for its return code.


### To use a company support address, set up forwarding


Start the forwarding rule in the shop mailbox. To check that a reply can travel in the other direction, open a different mailbox as the rider.


1. In the **Intercom owner’s window** , click the **Settings** gear at the bottom left. Expand **Channels** in the sidebar and select **Email** . On the **Domains & addresses** tab, find **Start email setup** and click **+ New email address** .


The black + New email address button is inside Start email setup. If the welcome banner is open, scroll past it to find the same card.


1. In the **Add email address** panel on the right, enter the shop’s support address on your work domain in **Your email address** . This is where customers will send their questions. Leave **Automatically forward emails from this address** on and click **Start setup for this address** .


The From and To lines show a sample email. The button below the orange switch is gray while the address field is empty.


Intercom excludes personal email addresses and Google Groups for custom forwarding. Copy the workspace receiving address shown in its forwarding instructions. This second address is the destination you enter at your mail provider.[Connect an email support channel](https://www.intercom.com/help/en/articles/9744849-connect-your-email-support-channel)


1. For an unused test address on a Google Workspace domain, an administrator can open **Apps → Google Workspace → Gmail → Default routing** , choose **Single recipient** and enter that exact test address. Under **Change envelope recipient** , replace the recipient with the Intercom address you copied. Save the rule, then use **Verify automatic forwarding** in Intercom. This lets you route one address on a catch-all domain without buying another mailbox or forwarding the rest of the domain’s mail.[Google’s single-address routing instructions](https://knowledge.workspace.google.com/admin/gmail/advanced/forward-email-to-a-third-party-crm)


### Find the customer’s email in Inbox


From your external mailbox, send a message to the address you chose. Use the subject **Bike light return** and ask **Which return label code do I use for my Larkspur M4 bike light repair?**


In Intercom, open **Inbox → All** and select **Bike light return** . Check that the contact is the customer who sent it and **To** shows the address they used. Leave this email unanswered while you give the Agent its repair policy. If a forwarded email shows the forwarding operator as the customer, check how your provider preserves the original sender.[How Intercom identifies forwarded customers](https://www.intercom.com/help/en/articles/7339364-detect-customers-in-forwarded-emails)


## 2. Give the AI a repair policy you can test


The shop sells a fictional **Larkspur M4 bike light** . Its repair code is deliberately distinctive. Put it in just one place, the Knowledge Base article. Leave it out of the customer’s question, the subject line and the Agent’s instructions. That gives you a way to recognize the article’s information in the eventual reply.


In **Quickchat AI** , select your connected Agent at the top left. If you’re starting fresh, choose **Set up manually** when creating your Agent and name it **Wheelhouse Repair** . Click **Knowledge Base** in the sidebar, then **Add Article** in the top row.[Quickchat AI Knowledge Base](https://quickchat.ai/docs/ai-agent/knowledge-base)


Choose Knowledge Base at the left, then Add Article at the top. The shop’s existing Saturday pickup article can stay where it is.


Enter **Larkspur M4 bike light repair returns** in **Title** . Paste both lines below into **Content** , click **Save** , and look for **Ready** beside the article in the list. A customer may receive anything written in this article, so use a policy the shop can share.


```text
For a Larkspur M4 bike light repair, the return label code is LILAC-27.
Write the code on the paper slip. Put the slip inside the battery compartment before packing the light.
```


Use Title for the product and Content for the two facts. Reopen the saved article to check the code and the packing instruction side by side.


Find the bike-light title in the article list and check for Ready before testing.


In **Conversations → Testing** , select **Create Dataset → Paste messages** . Name it **Wheelhouse email pilot: return code and packing** . Paste these three questions into the messages field with a line containing three hyphens between them. Each starts its own test conversation.[Simulation Testing in Quickchat AI](https://quickchat.ai/docs/conversations/testing)


```text
Which return label code do I use for my Larkspur M4 bike light repair?
---
Where should I put the paper slip for my Larkspur M4 bike light repair?
---
How much does the Larkspur M4 bike light repair cost?
```


Separate the questions with three hyphens on a line. Check that all three messages are present before saving.


Open **Evaluation criteria** . Require the exact current code for the first question, the battery compartment for the second, and an acknowledgment that the price needs confirmation for the third. Click **Create** . To try the questions, open the dataset, choose **Run** , review the credit estimate and click **Start Run** . Read the three answers individually. A price in the third answer is a reason to revisit the Agent’s instructions before connecting customer mail.


Read the messages on the saved dataset. The price question tests how the Agent answers when the shop has supplied no price.


If your Agent quotes a price, open **Identity → AI Persona → Main Prompt** and add the following sentence to its existing instructions. **Use the Knowledge Base for repair details. If it does not give a price, tell the customer the repair desk needs to confirm it.** Run the same questions again. Now the Agent has a policy it can use when you assign it the rider’s email.


### Set up the same test from ChatGPT or Claude


We used the Quickchat AI account connection to save this article and all three test questions on the existing Wheelhouse Agent. To do the same, connect your account in your preferred app, paste the article and questions above, then send the request below. Choose the Intercom assignee in Inbox. If you use a company support address, set up forwarding at your mail provider.[Quickchat AI for ChatGPT](https://chatgpt.com/plugins/plugin_asdk_app_6a4656c688748191be4c5247fb0d5dfc) ·[Quickchat AI for Claude](https://claude.ai/directory/connectors/app-quickchat-ai)


> Find my Wheelhouse Repair Agent. Add the attached Larkspur M4 bike light repair returns policy if it is missing. Create the three-question email test dataset if it does not exist. Read back the saved policy and questions before starting a run.


## 3. Assign one customer’s email to Quickchat AI


In Quickchat AI, open **External Apps** on the same Agent and choose **Intercom** . If the card shows **Reconnect** , read **Connected as** and use **Test connection** to check the named teammate. Wheelhouse already has a dedicated teammate called **Quickchat AI** . Keeping the same Agent preserves the connection used for Messenger. Connecting the same Intercom teammate to a different Agent moves that connection.[Quickchat AI’s Intercom channel](https://quickchat.ai/docs/channels/intercom)


Look in External Apps in the Agent sidebar, then open the Intercom card. The same connection can carry Messenger chats and email conversations.


For a new workspace, the owner opens **Settings → Workspace → Teammates** and invites a dedicated teammate with a full seat, Inbox access and permission to install apps. Accept the invitation in a second browser profile, sign in as that teammate, and select the correct Intercom workspace. In that profile, open the Quickchat AI Agent’s **External Apps → Intercom → Connect to Intercom** and authorize access. The name beside **Connected as** should match the person you’ll select in Inbox.[Step-by-step Intercom connection walkthrough](https://quickchat.ai/post/create-an-ai-chatbot-for-intercom-quickchat-ai-integration)


In the connected panel, turn **Enable Intercom** on and leave **Reply to all conversations** off. Set **Automatically close inactive conversations** to **Never** for the test so you have time to read and reply. Click **Test connection** . The confirmation names the authenticated teammate. You’ll select that same name on the rider’s email.


In our Wheelhouse workspace, the green Test connection message names the dedicated teammate. The control above it lets you limit which conversations receive AI replies.


### On Essential, assign the first email yourself


In **Intercom → Inbox → All** , reopen the unanswered **Bike light return** email from step 1. In the **Details** panel on the right, click **Assignee** , then choose the individual **Quickchat AI** teammate from **Assign to** .


After you choose Quickchat AI, its name appears beside Assignee and Intercom records the assignment in the conversation. The separate Team inbox field can still say Unassigned.


With the AI named as Assignee, you can go straight to step 4. If you want future emails from this sender assigned automatically, the following Workflow applies the same choice to new conversations.


### On Advanced or Expert, route the pilot sender automatically


In the Intercom owner’s window, open **Fin AI Agent → Workflows → + New workflow → Create from scratch** . Pick **Start of conversation → Customer sends their first message** and name the Workflow **Repairs email pilot** . In the trigger, choose **Email** as the only channel. Under the audience, set **Email To** to the dedicated repairs mailbox. In each test, put that address in the customer’s **To** field. Mail addressed to other desks stays outside this Workflow.[Intercom’s illustrated email Workflow guide](https://www.intercom.com/help/en/articles/12819765-how-to-set-up-email-workflows)


Read the diagram from the incoming email. The recipient chooses the desk. The sender determines who answers at that desk.


Add a **Branch** . On the matching path use the contact’s **Email is** condition with the exact address of your first customer, then **Assign** to the individual **Quickchat AI** teammate. On the other path, **Assign** to the human who owns the repairs desk. Check the two addresses before saving. **Email To** is where the rider wrote, and the contact’s **Email** is who wrote in.[Intercom’s channel and recipient filters](https://www.intercom.com/help/en/articles/6884847-omnichannel-support-for-workflows)


Keep the test audience out of other automatic replies, acknowledgments and assignment rules. If Fin is active, check its Simple deployment audience because it takes priority over overlapping Workflows. Choose **Set live** when the repairs address and both assignments are correct. To try the rule, send a fresh email from the test customer and check its individual assignee.[How Intercom prioritizes deployments](https://www.intercom.com/help/en/articles/11769044-introduction-to-deploy)


Using the[standalone Quickchat AI Email channel](https://quickchat.ai/docs/channels/email) instead? It gives you a Quickchat AI forwarding address. Here the customer writes to Intercom, either directly or through the shop’s mail provider. The team manages the conversation and posts public replies in Intercom Inbox.


## 4. Verify the public answer in Intercom Inbox


Stay in **Bike light return** . Read the public reply from **Quickchat AI** beneath the original question. Ours gave the code **LILAC-27** and told the rider to write it on the paper slip and put the slip **inside the battery compartment** . The yellow note in this conversation links to Quickchat AI for the team. The blue reply is the answer addressed to the rider.


In **Quickchat AI → Inbox** , open the matching Intercom conversation and compare the reply with the two lines you saved in step 2. The rider supplied the product name but neither policy detail. Finding both details in the public answer is how we checked that the shop’s Agent answered the right email with the right instructions.


### What did the customer receive?


When we first checked the customer’s Gmail, including Spam, we couldn’t find the AI reply. At **17:10 on November 25** , a teammate opened **Email** in the same Intercom conversation, checked the recipient and sent **Wheelhouse delivery check 1546** . A minute later, Intercom showed **Sending** .


After the teammate clicks Send in the Email composer, their message appears in the conversation. One minute later, Intercom still shows Sending beneath it.


The next morning, the customer found the human reply in their Gmail account using Apple Mail. The reply was timestamped **03:35 on November 26** , about 10 hours and 25 minutes after the teammate sent it. The cause of the delay is unknown. Delivery of the separate AI answer containing **LILAC-27** remains unconfirmed.


Match the message body to the reply in Intercom. Wheelhouse delivery check 1546 identifies the human message in the customer’s copy of the Bike light return thread.


### How to check threading when an email arrives


Use **Reply** on the received answer, then check that the follow-up appears in the *original* Intercom conversation. If a new conversation appeared, hover over the email icon on the incoming message in Intercom and select **View raw email** . Compare its **In-Reply-To** and **References** with the previous message’s **Message-ID** . These headers allow Intercom to connect related messages. Matching subjects or one folded conversation in Gmail can look convincing even when Intercom opened a second record.[How Intercom threads emails](https://www.intercom.com/help/en/articles/7996715-email-threading)


Use Reply to keep the packing question in the original Bike light return conversation (A1). Use Compose for A2 so the first code cannot influence the new answer.


## Optional experiment. Change the return code


To test a policy update, open the bike-light article in Quickchat AI, change **LILAC-27** to **LILAC-28** , save and wait for **Ready** . From your test mailbox, click **Compose** and use a new subject, **Return label for Larkspur M4, case A2** . Ask the original question without including either code. Assign the new conversation to Quickchat AI, then compare its public Intercom reply with the original **Bike light return** reply.


Edit just the last digit in Content. Leave the packing instructions and the customer’s question the same.


Our first public reply said **LILAC-27** . After the edit, look for **LILAC-28** in the new conversation. Changing one digit makes an old answer obvious, and starting a new thread keeps the old code out of the conversation history. If A2 still gives 27, check which Agent owns the channel, whether the edit is Ready and whether another article contains the old code. In Quickchat AI Inbox, open **Why AI said that** on the answer if available to inspect the source. We used the same fresh-conversation method to test a changed pickup window in our[HubSpot knowledge base walkthrough](https://quickchat.ai/post/hubspot-chatbot-knowledge-base) .


We restored **LILAC-27** in the demo Agent after capturing the article edit. When you finish your test, restore your original policy, take **Repairs email pilot** offline if you created it, and return open pilot conversations to the human teammate.


## Where to look when a reply goes missing


What you can see What to check next


The repairs mailbox received the request. Intercom Inbox is empty. Verify the provider’s automatic forwarding destination and confirmation. In Intercom open **All** , including closed conversations, and search for the unique case subject.


The email arrived in Intercom under the forwarding operator’s name. Compare the original sender on the forwarded email with the contact. Recheck provider-side automatic forwarding before switching on a sender-based rule.


Intercom has the right contact but the wrong assignee. Check **Email To** , the contact’s **Email** , the first-message trigger and the named individual. A broad rule can reclaim the conversation.


Quickchat Testing gives the code. The AI-assigned email is unanswered. Verify **Enable Intercom** , **Connected as** and the individual **Assignee** . Use a new unanswered message for the test. A public reply a teammate has already sent can prevent a duplicate answer.


There is a public reply in Intercom, but the external mailbox is empty. Check the outgoing recipient and look below the reply for a delivery-error note. **Not seen** means Intercom has not recorded an open. A reply marked **Sending** was still shown as sending when you looked. Check the original sender’s mailbox for a received copy.[Intercom’s Inbox delivery errors](https://www.intercom.com/help/en/articles/9465187-why-did-a-message-delivery-fail-from-the-inbox)


The answer arrived twice. Read both public authors. Check AI assignment, Fin’s audience and any Workflow that sends a separate acknowledgment. Leave only the intended responder on the pilot path.


The same customer’s second question opened a new conversation. Confirm the customer used **Reply** on the received message and inspect the threading headers on the follow-up.


## Frequently asked questions


### Can an AI answer Intercom support emails from a private knowledge base?


Yes. A customer emailed our Intercom workspace and the Quickchat AI teammate answered with the repair code and packing instruction from its knowledge base. You can compare the public reply in Intercom Inbox with the policy you gave the Agent.


### Can I try AI email replies on Intercom Essential?


Yes. In Intercom Inbox, open a fresh, unanswered email and use Assign to to select the individual Quickchat AI teammate. You can assign a second test email to a person yourself. Intercom offers the visual Workflows builder for automatic email assignment on Advanced and Expert.


### Do I need email forwarding to test AI replies in Intercom?


No. In Intercom, copy the Workspace email address from Settings → Channels → Email → Email settings. Send a test message directly to it from a mailbox you can open. To keep using a company support address, forward mail from that address to the destination Intercom provides.


### Can I use a personal Gmail address or a free Intercom developer workspace?


You can email the built-in workspace address from a personal Gmail account to test as a customer. For a custom support address, use a work-domain address. Intercom excludes personal addresses and Google Groups for custom forwarding. Its free developer workspaces disable outbound email, so use a regular workspace with outbound sending enabled to check what the customer receives.


### How do I keep other customers’ support emails with people?


Leave Reply to all conversations off in Quickchat AI. Assign individual emails to the AI in Intercom Inbox. To automate that choice, limit an Intercom Workflow to the test support address and the Email channel. Route your test sender to the AI teammate and other senders at that address to a person.


### Will the customer see the repairs address or the teammate’s address?


Intercom can send teammate replies from the original inbound address after the support address is verified and forwarded and its domain is authenticated. Select Inbound address under Teammate replies from, then expand the actual email in the customer’s mailbox. From identifies the visible sender. Reply-To may contain an Intercom address that routes replies into that conversation.


### Why does Quickchat AI pass Test connection but my customer has no email?


Test connection checks the connected teammate. To verify delivery, look for the text of the AI answer in the customer’s mailbox. In our test, a human reply marked Sending arrived overnight. The AI reply containing LILAC-27 was visible in Intercom and Quickchat AI. Its delivery to the customer remains unconfirmed.


### How do I check that a follow-up stayed in the same Intercom email thread?


Press Reply on the message received in the external mailbox. Check that the follow-up and answer appear both there and in the original Intercom conversation. If the conversation split, compare the incoming follow-up’s In-Reply-To and References headers with the Message-ID of the previous email.


### How can I tell that a reply used my latest knowledge base article?


Put a distinctive code in one article and keep it out of the prompt and customer question. After the first public answer appears in Intercom, edit the code, wait for Ready and compose a fresh email. Compare the replies in the two Intercom conversations and restore the original code.
